literal: Xiaojing Emperor bore the taboo name Shanjian; he was the heir of Prince Wenxuan of Qinghe, Dan; his mother was Consort Hu.
idiomatic: Xiaojing Emperor bore the taboo name Shanjian. He was heir to Prince Wenxuan of Qinghe, Dan; his mother was Lady Hu.

literal: In the third year of Yongxi he was appointed direct-palace scattered cavalier attendant; in the eighth month he was made general of agile cavalry, opening-office equal-to-three-division commander.
idiomatic: In the third year of Yongxi he became direct-palace scattered cavalier attendant; in the eighth month he was made general of agile cavalry with an opening office equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.

literal: When the emperor who had gone west had entered the passes, Gao Huan (Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu) went to welcome him but could not succeed; he then met with the hundred officials in council and set up the emperor to continue the line after Emperor Suzong—he was eleven years old.
idiomatic: After the western-departing emperor entered the passes, Gao Huan (Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu) tried to welcome him back and failed. He then convened the ministers and enthroned the boy to carry on the line of Emperor Suzong—eleven years old.

literal: Tenth month of winter, day bingyin: he took the throne in the northeast of the city, granted a general amnesty to all under Heaven, and changed the third year of Yongxi to the first year of Tianping.
idiomatic: On bingyin day in the tenth month of winter he was enthroned in the northeast of the city, amnestied the realm, and renamed the third year of Yongxi the first year of Tianping.

literal: Day gengwu: Grand Preceptor, Prince of Zhao Commandery Chen was made grand marshal; Minister of Works, Prince of Xianyang Tan was made grand commander; opening-office equal-to-three-division commander Gao Sheng was made minister over the masses; opening-office equal-to-three-division commander Gao Ang was made minister of works.
idiomatic: On gengwu day Grand Preceptor Chen, prince of Zhao commandery, became grand marshal; Minister of Works Tan, prince of Xianyang, became grand commander; Gao Sheng and Gao Ang, both opening-office equals to the Three Excellencies, became minister over the masses and minister of works.

literal: Day renshen: there was a service at the Grand Temple.
idiomatic: On renshen day the court performed rites at the Grand Temple.

literal: An edict said: "Settled settlement can yet be moved—an enlightened canon since antiquity;
idiomatic: An edict said: "A settled people may still be moved—that is an enlightened rule from antiquity;

literal: dwelling without fixed abode was a settled practice of former ages.
idiomatic: and to dwell without a fixed seat was a settled practice of former ages.

literal: Therefore the Yin moved through eight cities and the Zhou divined three sites.
idiomatic: Thus the Yin shifted among eight cities and the Zhou divined three sites.

literal: Fortune and misfortune have their measure; rise and decline have no constancy.
idiomatic: Fortune and misfortune have their measure; rise and decline know no constancy.

literal: Matters arise from change and adaptation; principle comes from what cannot be avoided.
idiomatic: Matters arise from change and adaptation; principle comes from what cannot be avoided.

literal: Grand Ancestor Emperor Xiaowen observed the signs of Heaven and bowed to human counsel; he set out from Wuzhou and came to Song county—though Wei was an old realm, its mandate was made new.
idiomatic: Grand Ancestor Emperor Xiaowen read the signs of Heaven and bowed to human counsel; he set out from Wuzhou and came to Song county—Wei was an old state, but its mandate was made new.

literal: By the end of Zhengguang the state's steps were perilously narrow; mourning and disorder did not cease, bandits and enemies invaded together, so that our living people had nowhere to set hand or foot.
idiomatic: By the end of Zhengguang the throne was in dire straits; mourning and disorder never ceased, and raiders pressed from every side, until the people had nowhere to turn.

literal: Now, far following the ancient pattern and deeply testing present affairs, we have divined the tortoise and inherited good fortune: the capital is moved to the Zhang and Fen rivers.
idiomatic: Now, following the ancient pattern and testing the times, we have divined the tortoise and taken good fortune—the capital moves to the Zhang and Fen rivers.

literal: May we thereby further found the great foundation and again make the imperial calendar flourish.
idiomatic: May we thereby enlarge the great foundation and make the imperial calendar flourish again.

literal: Let those in charge set out regulations clearly and set out on the road in good time.
idiomatic: Let the responsible offices draw up rules clearly and set out on the road in good time.

literal: " Day bingzi: the imperial carriage moved the capital north to Ye.
idiomatic: On bingzi day the imperial carriage moved the capital north to Ye.

literal: An edict ordered Gao Huan (Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu) to remain behind and divide the host.
idiomatic: An edict ordered Gao Huan (Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu) to stay behind and divide the forces.

literal: Si Province was renamed Luo Province; Defender of the Realm, Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Bi was made general of agile cavalry, equal-to-three-division commander, and regional inspector of Luo, garrisoning Luoyang.
idiomatic: Si province was renamed Luo province; Yuan Bi, defender of the realm and director of the Masters of Writing, was made general of agile cavalry, equal-to-three-division commander, and inspector of Luo, to garrison Luoyang.

literal: An edict: households that followed the move and the hundred officials were granted tax remission for three years; settled residents for five years.
idiomatic: An edict granted three years' tax remission to households that moved with the court and to officials, and five years to residents who stayed put.

literal: Second year, first month of spring: Baoju's inspector of Wei Prefecture Kezhun Hun Daoyuan led his command in surrender; Gao Huan (Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu) received and settled them and relieved their grain stores.
idiomatic: In the second year, first month of spring, Kezhun Hun Daoyuan, inspector of Wei under Baoju, led his command in surrender; Gao Huan (Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu) received them, settled them, and opened the granaries.

literal: Day jisi: an edict made Gao Huan (Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu) grand chancellor, with borrowed yellow battle-axe, sword and shoes in the hall, and no need to hurry in court audience; the rest remained as before.
idiomatic: On jisi day an edict made Gao Huan (Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu) grand chancellor, lending the yellow battle-axe, permission to wear sword and shoes in the hall, and exemption from hurrying at audience; other honors stood unchanged.

literal: The prince firmly declined and did not accept.
idiomatic: The prince firmly declined and would not accept.

literal: Day yihai: Concurrent Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Southeastern-route grand mobile office Yuan Yan campaigned against Yuan Qinghe, defeated him, and put him to flight.
idiomatic: On yihai day Yuan Yan, concurrent vice director and southeastern-route grand mobile office, campaigned against Yuan Qinghe, routed him, and drove him off.

literal: Second month, day renwu: Grand Commander, Prince of Xianyang Tan was made grand preceptor; Regional Inspector of Si Province, Prince of Xihe Cong was made grand commander.
idiomatic: In the second month, on renwu day, Tan, prince of Xianyang and grand commander, became grand preceptor; Cong, prince of Xihe and inspector of Si, became grand commander.

literal: Day jichou: former southern inspector of Qing Province Daye Ba beheaded Fan Zihe and surrendered; Yan Province was pacified.
idiomatic: On jichou day Daye Ba, former southern inspector of Qing, beheaded Fan Zihe and surrendered; Yan province was pacified.

literal: Day wuxu: Xiao Yan's inspector of Si Province Chen Qingzhi raided Yu Province; Inspector Yao Xiong struck and drove him off.
idiomatic: On wuxu day Chen Qingzhi, inspector of Si under Xiao Yan, raided Yu; Inspector Yao Xiong beat him back.

literal: Third month, day xinyou: Minister over the Masses Gao Sheng was made grand commander; Minister of Works Gao Ang was made minister over the masses; Prince of Jiyin Huiye was made minister of works.
idiomatic: In the third month, on xinyou day, Gao Sheng became grand commander, Gao Ang minister over the masses, and Huiye, prince of Jiyin, minister of works.

literal: Gao Huan (Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu) campaigned against and pacified the Mountain Hu Liu Lixing and beheaded him.
idiomatic: Gao Huan (Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu) suppressed the Mountain Hu Liu Lixing and beheaded him.

literal: His son, the self-styled Prince of Nanhai, again usurped the imperial title; Gao Huan (Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu) advanced, attacked, broke him, and captured him, together with his younger brother the self-styled Prince of Xihai, the empress, ladies, and more than four hundred persons below them, and also more than twenty thousand households of fugitives.
idiomatic: His son, who had styled himself Prince of Nanhai, again claimed the throne; Gao Huan (Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu) advanced, broke him, and took him prisoner, with his brother the self-styled Prince of Xihai, the empress, consorts, and more than four hundred persons besides, and over twenty thousand fugitive households.

literal: Day xinwei: because of drought, an edict ordered the capital and all provinces, commanderies, and counties to gather and bury exposed bones.
idiomatic: On xinwei day, because of drought, an edict ordered the capital and every province, commandery, and county to gather and bury exposed bones.

literal: That spring, Koguryŏ and Khitan both sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: That spring Koguryŏ and the Khitan both sent envoys with tribute.

literal: [4] Former inspector of Qing Province Hou Yuan rebelled and raided Qing and Qi.
idiomatic: [4] Hou Yuan, former inspector of Qing, rebelled and raided Qing and Qi.

literal: Day guimao: Inspector of Ji Province Cai Jun campaigned against and pacified him.
idiomatic: On guimao day Cai Jun, inspector of Ji, campaigned against him and pacified the region.

literal: Day renchen: prisoners held for audience at the capital were released.
idiomatic: On renchen day prisoners awaiting audience at the capital were released.

literal: Fifth month: great drought; at city gates, palace gates, and the gates of ministries, offices, temples, agencies, and wards people were made to pour water—without exempting kings and dukes, with no limit of days, until rain came and then it stopped.
idiomatic: In the fifth month a great drought struck; at every city gate, palace gate, and ministry, office, temple, agency, and ward gate water was poured—princes and dukes not excepted—with no day-limit until rain fell.

literal: Sixth month: Yuan Qinghe raided southern Yu Province; Inspector Yao Xiong greatly defeated him.
idiomatic: In the sixth month Yuan Qinghe raided southern Yu; Inspector Yao Xiong routed him.

literal: Seventh month of autumn, day jiaxu: Chuo, grandson of Prince of Runan Yue, was enfeoffed as Prince of Langye.
idiomatic: On jiaxu day in the seventh month of autumn, Chuo, grandson of Yue, prince of Runan, was enfeoffed prince of Langye.

literal: Eighth month, day xinmao: Minister of Works, Prince of Jiyin Huiye was removed from office for an offense.
idiomatic: In the eighth month, on xinmao day, Huiye, prince of Jiyin and minister of works, was dismissed for an offense.

literal: Day jiawu: seventy-six thousand men were levied to build the new palace.
idiomatic: On jiawu day seventy-six thousand men were levied to build the new palace.

literal: Ninth month: Gao Huan (Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu), because many officials who governed the people did not uphold the law, requested that upright court gentlemen be chosen—one sent to each province—to inquire into hardship and suffering.
idiomatic: In the ninth month Gao Huan (Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu), finding that many magistrates broke the law, asked that upright court gentlemen be chosen, one per province, to inquire into the people's hardships.

literal: Day dingsi: opening-office equal-to-three-division commander, Prince of Xiangcheng Xu was made minister of works.
idiomatic: On dingsi day Xu, prince of Xiangcheng and opening-office equal to the Three Excellencies, became minister of works.

literal: Eleventh month of winter, day dingwei: Xiao Yan's general Liu Zhongli raided Jing Province; Inspector Wang Yuan struck and defeated him.
idiomatic: On dingwei day in the eleventh month of winter, Liu Zhongli, a general of Xiao Yan, raided Jing; Inspector Wang Yuan defeated him.

literal: [5] Day guichou: the Round Mound was sacrificed to.
idiomatic: [5] On guichou day sacrifice was offered at the Round Mound.

literal: Day jiayin: the Gate of Heaven and Earth burned; a dragon appeared in a well at a house in Bing Province.
idiomatic: On jiayin day the Gate of Heaven and Earth burned; a dragon was seen in a household well in Bing province.

literal: Day bingyin: an edict ordered Gao Cheng (Wenxiang) to begin his career as scattered cavalier attendant, general of agile cavalry, left grandee of splendid appearance, equal-to-three-division commander, and Duke of Taiyuan Commandery, state-founding, with a fief of three thousand households.
idiomatic: On bingyin day an edict launched Gao Cheng (Wenxiang) as scattered cavalier attendant, general of agile cavalry, left grandee of splendid appearance, equal-to-three-division commander, and state-founding duke of Taiyuan commandery, with a fief of three thousand households.

literal: Twelfth month, day renwu: the imperial carriage hunted east of Ye.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on renwu day, the emperor hunted east of Ye.

literal: Day jiawu: civil and military officials of every rank were given salary according to their posts.
idiomatic: On jiawu day civil and military officials of every rank received salary according to their posts.

literal: Third year, first month of spring, new moon on guimao: the hundred ministers were feasted in the front hall.
idiomatic: In the third year, on the guimao new moon of the first month of spring, the ministers were feasted in the front hall.

literal: Day wushen: an edict ordered the hundred officials to recommend scholars; those who recommended unworthy men were twice dismissed.
idiomatic: On wushen day an edict ordered officials to recommend scholars; recommenders of unworthy men were dismissed twice.

literal: Gao Huan (Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu) raided Baoju's Western Xia Province and took it.
idiomatic: Gao Huan (Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu) raided Western Xia under Baoju and took it.

literal: An edict added the nine bestowals for Gao Huan (Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu); Attendant-in-ordinary Yuan Zisi was sent to press the grant.
idiomatic: An edict offered Gao Huan (Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu) the nine bestowals; Attendant-in-ordinary Yuan Zisi was sent to press him to accept.

literal: He firmly declined and it was stopped.
idiomatic: He firmly declined and the grant was withdrawn.

literal: Second month, day dingwei: Xiao Yan's inspector of Guang Province Hao Shu brought his province in to submit.
idiomatic: In the second month, on dingwei day, Hao Shu, inspector of Guang under Xiao Yan, brought his province in.

literal: Day dingyou: an edict added for Gao Cheng (Wenxiang) commissioner with full powers, Director of the Masters of Writing, grand mobile office, and commander-in-chief; all Xianbei and Gaoche chiefs and commoners were placed under him.
idiomatic: On dingyou day an edict added for Gao Cheng (Wenxiang) commissioner with full powers, director of the Masters of Writing, grand mobile office, and commander-in-chief, with all Xianbei and Gaoche chiefs and tribesmen placed under his command.

literal: Third month, day jiayin: opening-office equal-to-three-division commander, Prince of Huashan Zhi was made grand marshal.
idiomatic: In the third month, on jiayin day, Zhi, prince of Huashan and opening-office equal to the Three Excellencies, became grand marshal.

literal: Day dingmao: Administrator of Yangxia Lu Gongzuan held the southern part of the commandery in rebellion; Commander-in-chief Yuan Zheng defeated him.
idiomatic: On dingmao day Lu Gongzuan, administrator of Yangxia, rebelled in the south of the commandery; Commander-in-chief Yuan Zheng defeated him.

literal: Fourth month of summer, day dingyou: Prince of Changle Dan died.
idiomatic: On dingyou day in the fourth month of summer, Dan, prince of Changle, died.

literal: Fifth month, day guimao: widowers, widows, orphans, solitaries, and the poor were given clothing in differing amounts.
idiomatic: In the fifth month, on guimao day, widowers, widows, orphans, solitaries, and the destitute received clothing in graded amounts.

literal: Day bingchen: Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Xihe Cong was made regional inspector of Si Province.
idiomatic: On bingchen day Cong, prince of Xihe and recorder of the Masters of Writing, became inspector of Si province.

literal: Day wuchen: Grand Commander Gao Sheng died.
idiomatic: On wuchen day Grand Commander Gao Sheng died.

literal: Sixth month, day xinsi: Prince of Zhao Commandery Chen died.
idiomatic: In the sixth month, on xinsi day, Chen, prince of Zhao commandery, died.

literal: Seventh month of autumn, day gengzi: a general amnesty was granted to all under Heaven.
idiomatic: On gengzi day in the seventh month of autumn the realm was amnestied.

literal: Xiao Yan's inspector of Xia Province Tian Dubi and the defense commander of Yingchuan Liu Luanqing both brought their provinces in to submit.
idiomatic: Tian Dubi, inspector of Xia under Xiao Yan, and Liu Luanqing, defense commander of Yingchuan, both brought their provinces in.

literal: Eighth month: Bing, Xi, Fen, and Jian provinces had frost fall; [6] great famine.
idiomatic: [6] In the eighth month Bing, Xi, Fen, and Jian provinces had frost; famine followed.

literal: Ninth month, day renyin: Inspector of Ding Province Hou Jing was made concurrent Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and southern-route grand mobile office, directing all armies in the southern campaign.
idiomatic: In the ninth month, on renyin day, Hou Jing, inspector of Ding, became concurrent vice director and southern-route grand mobile office, directing the southern armies.

literal: Day bingchen: Lu Jili of Yangping gathered a band and rebelled.
idiomatic: On bingchen day Lu Jili of Yangping raised a band and rebelled.

literal: Day xinyou: Censor-in-chief Dou Tai campaigned against and pacified him.
idiomatic: On xinyou day Censor-in-chief Dou Tai suppressed him.

literal: That year the state of Koguryŏ sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: That year Koguryŏ sent envoys with tribute.

literal: Fourth year, first month of spring: on the fifteenth day stealing games were forbidden.
idiomatic: In the fourth year, first month of spring, stealing games on the fifteenth were forbidden.

literal: Dou Tai, having met defeat, killed himself.
idiomatic: Dou Tai, defeated, killed himself.

literal: Day dingsi: Gao Aocao attacked Shangluo, took it, and captured Baoju's general of agile cavalry, regional inspector of Luo Quan Qi.
idiomatic: On dingsi day Gao Aocao took Shangluo and captured Quan Qi, Baoju's general of agile cavalry and inspector of Luo.

literal: [7] According to Zhang's collation this reading is correct; the text is now amended in accordance with the Book of Zhou.
idiomatic: [7] Collation note: Zhang's reading is accepted here; the text follows the Book of Zhou.

literal: Prince of Ruyang Xian was made recorder of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: Xian, prince of Ruyang, was made recorder of the Masters of Writing.

literal: Fourth month of summer, day xinwei: the spirit tablets of seven emperors were moved into the new temple; a general amnesty was granted to all under Heaven; civil and military officials within and without were all advanced one rank.
idiomatic: On xinwei day in the fourth month of summer the spirit tablets of seven emperors entered the new temple; the realm was amnestied and every official within and without the court was promoted one rank.

literal: Earlier, Zhang Jian of Xingyang and others had gathered a band and rebelled on Mount Daqi, communicating with Baoju.
idiomatic: Earlier Zhang Jian of Xingyang and others had raised a band on Mount Daqi in communication with Baoju.

literal: Day renchen: Martial Guard General Gao Yuansheng campaigned against and defeated them.
idiomatic: On renchen day Martial Guard General Gao Yuansheng defeated them.

literal: [8] Sixth month, day jisi: the emperor visited Hualin Park to judge lawsuits.
idiomatic: [8] In the sixth month, on jisi day, the emperor heard lawsuits at Hualin Park.

literal: Day xinwei: an edict ordered the Masters of Writing to gather exposed bones and bury flesh; prisoners were reviewed and recorded.
idiomatic: On xinwei day an edict ordered the Masters of Writing to bury the dead and review prisoners.

literal: Day renwu: the Gate of Heaven and Earth burned.
idiomatic: On renwu day the Gate of Heaven and Earth burned.

literal: Earlier, Xiao Yan, through Inspector of Yi Province Fu He, had requested friendly relations.
idiomatic: Earlier Xiao Yan, through Fu He, inspector of Yi, had sought friendly relations.

literal: Seventh month of autumn, day jiachen: Concurrent Scattered Cavalier Attendant Li Xie, [9] Concurrent Director of Personnel Lu Yuanming, and Concurrent Direct-palace Scattered Cavalier Attendant Li Ye were sent as envoys to Xiao Yan.
idiomatic: On jiachen day in the seventh month of autumn Li Xie, concurrent scattered cavalier attendant, [9] Lu Yuanming, concurrent director of personnel, and Li Ye, concurrent direct-palace scattered cavalier attendant, were sent to Xiao Yan.

literal: Eighth month: Baoju and Yuwen Heitu raided Shaan Province; the city fell and Inspector Li Huibo was killed by Heitu.
idiomatic: In the eighth month Baoju and Yuwen Heitu raided Shaan; the city fell and Inspector Li Huibo was slain by Heitu.

literal: Ninth month: Attendant-in-ordinary Yuan Zisi plotted with his nephew Zihua to enter the west; both were granted death.
idiomatic: In the ninth month Yuan Zisi plotted with his nephew Zihua to flee west; both were put to death.

literal: Intercalary month, day yichou: Defender General, Right Grandee of Splendid Appearance Jiang Tianle plotted rebellion and was executed.
idiomatic: On yichou day in the intercalary month Jiang Tianle, defender general and right grandee of splendid appearance, plotted rebellion and was executed.

literal: Selling wine in the capital was forbidden.
idiomatic: The sale of wine in the capital was forbidden.

literal: The text is deficient.
idiomatic: The text is deficient.

literal: Tenth month of winter: Prince of Xianyang Tan was made recorder of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter Tan, prince of Xianyang, was made recorder of the Masters of Writing.

literal: Day renchen: Gao Huan (Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu) campaigned west, reached Shazhou, could not take it, and returned.
idiomatic: On renchen day Gao Huan (Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu) marched west to Shazhou, failed to win, and turned back.

literal: Day jiyou: Baoju's grand mobile office Gong Jingshou and Commander Yang Baiju raided Luo Province; Commander-in-chief Han Yan greatly defeated them.
idiomatic: On jiyou day Gong Jingshou, Baoju's grand mobile office, and Commander Yang Baiju raided Luo; Commander-in-chief Han Yan routed them.

literal: [11] Baoju again sent his son, grand mobile office Yuan Jihai, and Commander-in-chief Dugu Ruyuan to press Luo Province; Inspector, Prince of Guangyang Zhan abandoned the city and withdrew; Jihai and Ruyuan then held Jinyong.
idiomatic: [11] Baoju again sent his son Yuan Jihai, grand mobile office, and Commander-in-chief Dugu Ruyuan against Luo; Zhan, prince of Guangyang and inspector, abandoned the city; Jihai and Ruyuan then held Jinyong.

literal: Chief clerk of Ying Province He Ruo Wei seized Inspector Tian Xun and rebelled westward; [12] he brought in Baoju's commander Liang Hui to hold the city.
idiomatic: He Ruo Wei, chief clerk of Ying, seized Inspector Tian Xun and rebelled west, [12] bringing in Baoju's commander Liang Hui to hold the city.

literal: Baoju again sent his commanders Zhao Jizong, Right Assistant Director Wei Xiaokuan, and others to attack and take Yu Province.
idiomatic: Baoju again sent Zhao Jizong, Wei Xiaokuan, and others to take Yu.

literal: Eleventh month, day bingzi: General of Agile Cavalry, Equal-to-three-division Commander Wanqi Pu was made grand commander.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on bingzi day, Wanqi Pu, general of agile cavalry and equal to the Three Excellencies, became grand commander.

literal: Twelfth month, day jiayin: Xiao Yan sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jiayin day, Xiao Yan sent envoys with tribute.

literal: Xing Mo of Hejian and Lu Zhongli of Fanyang each gathered bands and rebelled.
idiomatic: Xing Mo of Hejian and Lu Zhongli of Fanyang each raised bands in rebellion.

literal: That year Koguryŏ and Rouran both sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: That year Koguryŏ and Rouran both sent envoys with tribute.

literal: Fourth month of summer, day gengyin: a partial amnesty within the capital region.
idiomatic: On gengyin day in the fourth month of summer the capital region received a partial amnesty.

literal: Day renchen: Gao Huan (Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu) returned to Jinyang and requested that the ban on wine be lifted.
idiomatic: On renchen day Gao Huan (Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu) returned to Jinyang and asked that the wine ban be lifted.

literal: Sixth month, day renchen: the emperor visited Hualin Metropolitan Hall to hear lawsuits.
idiomatic: In the sixth month, on renchen day, the emperor heard lawsuits at Hualin Metropolitan Hall.
